summary: Taiwan waives visas for around 60 nationalities — 90 days for the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand among others — with free online travel authorisations or eVisas for several more. Remaining nationalities apply for a visitor visa at a Taipei representative office, and mainland Chinese travelers need special entry permits.

declarations.name: Taiwan Arrival Card
declarations.text: Foreign visitors without an Alien Resident Certificate, resident visa or diplomatic ID must submit the online Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC) on the National Immigration Agency's site within 7 days before arrival. Hong Kong, Macao and mainland travellers holding multiple-entry permits must submit it too.

source.name: National Immigration Agency (Taiwan) — Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC)

conflict.name: UK FCDO — Taiwan travel advice, entry requirements
conflict.states: Submit the TWAC within three days before arrival

currencyLimits.text: Cash over USD 10,000 (or over TWD 100,000 in local currency) must be declared on arrival. Confirm current thresholds with Taiwan Customs before carrying large sums.

source.name: UK FCDO — Taiwan travel advice (entry requirements)

notes: Bringing in meat products is banned under African swine fever controls — undeclared pork products carry very heavy fines.
Duty-free allowances for adults are 1 liter of alcohol and 200 cigarettes.
Fresh fruit and plants may not be brought in without quarantine clearance.

payments.text: Cards and mobile payments are widely accepted in cities, but night markets, small eateries and taxis often want cash. An EasyCard covers the metro, buses and convenience-store purchases.

safety.text: Taiwan is one of Asia's safest destinations, with very low crime. The main considerations are natural: typhoons from July to September and occasional earthquakes.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Taiwan travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: Fall (October-November) and spring (March-April) bring mild, drier weather; summer is hot and humid with typhoon risk from July to September.

tips.text: Visa-free travelers must hold a confirmed onward or return ticket — airlines routinely refuse boarding without one.
Typhoons strike between July and September and can shut transport and east-coast attractions for days — build slack into itineraries and monitor Central Weather Administration warnings.
Do not bring any meat products into Taiwan, even sealed snacks — African swine fever controls mean undeclared pork items attract fines running to hundreds of thousands of NT dollars.
Buy an EasyCard at any metro station or convenience store. It works on the Taipei and Kaohsiung metros, buses, trains and in shops, and makes getting around effortless.
Submit the online Taiwan Arrival Card within 7 days before you arrive — it replaces the paper form and speeds up immigration.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Taiwan?
faq.answer: Around 60 nationalities do not: the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and others get 90 days visa-free; Singapore, Malaysia, the Dominican Republic, Belize, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines get 30 days; and Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei and Oman get 14 days. About 20 nationalities, including the Gulf states, can apply online for an eVisa, and India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam can use a free online travel authorization if they hold visas from designated countries. Everyone else applies for a visitor visa at a Taipei representative office.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Taiwan?
faq.answer: US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days with a confirmed onward or return ticket. The visa-exempt stay cannot normally be extended — leaving and re-entering resets the clock.

faq.question: Can mainland Chinese citizens visit Taiwan?
faq.answer: Not as ordinary tourists at present. Mainland residents need entry permits issued by both sides, individual tourist travel has been suspended since 2019, and only limited categories such as business, family visits and approved group programs are processed.

faq.question: Do Hong Kong and Macao residents need a visa for Taiwan?
faq.answer: Not a visa — eligible Hong Kong and Macao permanent residents apply online for an entry permit through Taiwan's National Immigration Agency, which allows a stay of up to 30 days from the day after entry.

faq.question: Do I need an onward ticket to enter Taiwan visa-free?
faq.answer: Yes. A confirmed onward or return ticket is a condition of visa-free entry, and airlines check it at check-in. One-way travelers should obtain a visitor visa instead.
